```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  echo    = FALSE,
  warning = FALSE,
  message = FALSE,
  out.width = "100%"
)

suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(dplyr)
  library(tidyr)
  library(ggplot2)
  library(ggrepel)
  library(paletteer)
  library(DT)
  library(gridExtra)
  library(stringr)
})

source('rer_contract.R')
.style <- if(file.exists('report_style.R')) 'report_style.R' else '../../TRAIT_ANALYSIS/local/src/report_style.R'
source(.style)
set_report_style()
.tableau10 <- report_palette(10)
if (!file.exists(params$continuous_rds)) stop('RER result RDS not found')
rer_verify_snapshot(params$continuous_rds)
res <- rer_results(readRDS(params$continuous_rds))
.recorded <- attr(res,'rer_report_metadata')
.settings <- attr(res,'rer_settings')
# Restore producer metadata before rendering any prose; never consult SCORING files.
.pe <- knitr::knit_global()
.locked <- bindingIsLocked('params',.pe)
if (.locked) unlockBinding('params',.pe)
if (!is.null(.recorded)) {
  params$traitname <- .recorded$traitname
  params$pval_threshold <- .recorded$nominal_threshold
  params$fdr_threshold <- .recorded$fdr_threshold
}
params$analysis_mode <- if(!is.null(attr(res,'rer_type'))) attr(res,'rer_type') else if(!is.null(.settings$mode)) .settings$mode else 'unknown'
params$trait_transform <- if(!is.null(.settings$transformation$effective)) .settings$transformation$effective else 'unknown'
if (.locked) lockBinding('params',.pe)
n_perms_total <- attr(res,'n_perms')
rer_df <- rer_summary(res,params$pval_threshold,params$fdr_threshold)
has_perm <- any(!is.na(rer_df$p.perm))
fmt_pperm <- function(x) ifelse(is.na(x),NA_character_,as.character(signif(x,3)))

```

---

## Overview

This report summarises the results of **RERconverge** (relative evolutionary rate convergence;
Kowalczyk _et al._, 2019) applied in **`r params$analysis_mode`** mode to **`r params$traitname`**.

RERconverge tests associations between **relative evolutionary rates (RERs)** and
phenotype paths. In continuous mode, `char2Paths(metric="diff")` reconstructs ancestral
values and uses descendant minus ancestor changes, mapped onto the master-tree paths.
**Positive rho** associates higher RER with more positive phenotype changes;
**negative rho** associates higher RER with more negative changes. These are relative
rate associations, not absolute rates, temporal acceleration, or evidence of positive selection.
For a binary phenotype, the direction instead refers to the encoded foreground (1) versus background (0).

The analysis uses the following key statistics:

| Statistic | Meaning |
|-----------|---------|
| **Rho** | Signed association: Pearson in continuous mode; the binary association depends on its configured test |
| **N** | Number of matched, non-missing path observations used for the gene; not necessarily the number of species |
| **P** | Raw analytic p-value of the association test |
| **p.adj** | BH-adjusted analytic P from the RER producer |
| **p.perm** | Native `permpvalcor()` empirical p: choose the side of the gene-specific null median containing observed rho; count equally or more extreme null rho on that side, then (k+1)/(d+1), where d counts null rho on that side including median ties. NA null values are removed per gene. This evaluates either direction; it is not the absolute-value tail used by FCS. |
| **p.perm.adj** | BH adjustment of available gene p.perm values in the original RER family, before any directional or cross-method subset |

> **Calls are nominal:** `Call` and the directional lists use `p.perm < pval_threshold`,
> without multiple-testing correction. **BH empirical** separately marks
> `p.perm.adj < fdr_threshold`. Unavailable empirical evidence remains NA and is not
> a measured negative result. Analytic P supplies the signed global FCS ranking
> `sign(Rho) × −log10(P)`; gene p.perm and pathway p.perm are different tests.
> FCS retains one global signed ranking and a bilateral contrast. Its direction is
> the sign of the set statistic (AUC − 0.5), not the sign of every member gene.
> RER positive/negative must not be relabelled CAAS top/bottom.
> Gene direction uses sign(Rho); native `permpvalcor$permstats` instead uses
> sign(Rho − median(null)). These need not agree near zero.

Analytic and empirical inference can disagree in either direction (Saputra et al. 2021).
The minimum observed p below is descriptive; a theoretical floor requires the valid
null counts and median ties of each gene. The binary marine example in Saputra Fig. 5C
is not a universal minimum number of permulations for continuous phenotypes.

## Gene-level Summary

```{r gene-table}
display_df <- rer_df %>%
  mutate(
    Rho   = round(Rho, 4),
    P     = signif(P,    3),
    p.adj = signif(p.adj, 3),
    p.perm = if (has_perm) signif(p.perm, 3) else NA_real_,
    p.perm.adj = if (has_perm) signif(p.perm.adj, 3) else NA_real_
  )

# Include p.perm column only when permutations were run
if (has_perm) {
  display_df <- display_df %>%
    select(gene, Rho, N, P, p.adj, p.perm, p.perm.adj, `Empirical available`, `BH empirical`, Call) %>%
    rename(Gene = gene, `Raw P (parametric)` = P, `p.adj (parametric BH)` = p.adj,
           `p.perm (permulation)` = p.perm, `p.perm.adj (permulation BH)` = p.perm.adj)
} else {
  display_df <- display_df %>%
    select(gene, Rho, N, P, p.adj, `Empirical available`, `BH empirical`, Call) %>%
    rename(Gene = gene, `Raw P (parametric)` = P, `p.adj (parametric BH)` = p.adj)
}

DT::datatable(
  display_df,
  filter   = "top",
  rownames = FALSE,
  options  = list(pageLength = 30, scrollX = TRUE),
  caption  = htmltools::tags$caption(
    style = "caption-side: top; text-align: left; font-weight: bold;",
    sprintf(
      "RERconverge gene-level results (Call = nominal empirical; BH empirical = adjusted) | Trait: %s",
      params$traitname
    )
  )
) %>%
  DT::formatStyle(
    "Call",
    backgroundColor = DT::styleEqual(
      c("Positively correlated", "Negatively correlated", "Significant", ""),
      c("#ffe0e0",               "#dff0ff",               "#fff0d0",      "white")
    )
  ) %>% DT::formatStyle("BH empirical", fontWeight=DT::styleEqual(c(TRUE,FALSE),c("bold","normal")), backgroundColor=DT::styleEqual(c(TRUE,FALSE),c("#FFE5A0","white")))
```

Machine-readable tables and gene lists are produced and validated independently of this report.

## Visualisations

### Correlation plot

```{r corr-plot, fig.height=7, fig.width=9}
label_df <- rer_df %>%
  filter(signif) %>%
  arrange(if (has_perm) p.perm else p.adj) %>%
  slice_head(n = params$top_n_labels)

ggplot(rer_df, aes(x = Rho, y = -log10(if (has_perm) p.perm else (P + 1e-300)))) +
  geom_point(
    aes(colour = case_when(
      pos_corr ~ "Positively correlated",
      neg_corr ~ "Negatively correlated",
      signif   ~ "Significant",
      TRUE     ~ "Non-significant"
    )),
    alpha = 0.7,
    size  = 2
  ) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dotted", colour = "grey60", linewidth = 0.5) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = -log10(params$pval_threshold),
             linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey40", linewidth = 0.5) +
  geom_text_repel(
    data    = label_df,
    aes(label = gene),
    size    = 3,
    max.overlaps = 30
  ) +
  scale_colour_manual(
    values = c(
      "Positively correlated" = .tableau10[3],
      "Negatively correlated" = .tableau10[1],
      "Significant"           = .tableau10[2],
      "Non-significant"       = "grey60"
    ),
    name = NULL
  ) +
  labs(
    title    = paste("RERconverge correlation plot — Trait:", params$traitname),
    subtitle = paste0("n = ", nrow(rer_df), " genes"),
    x        = if(params$analysis_mode=="binary") "Signed binary association (rho)" else "Pearson correlation with phenotype paths (rho)",
    y        = if (has_perm) expression(-log[10](p.perm)) else expression(-log[10](P))
  ) +
  report_theme(base_size = 13) +
  theme(legend.position = "top")
```

### Permutation p-values

```{r perm-plot, fig.height=6, fig.width=10, eval=has_perm}
# P vs p.perm scatter — genes on the diagonal have consistent parametric
# and empirical evidence; off-diagonal genes may be driven by phylogenetic structure.
perm_label_df <- rer_df %>%
  filter(signif) %>%
  arrange(p.perm) %>%
  slice_head(n = params$top_n_labels)

# Descriptive minimum only: do not infer a theoretical floor from this table.
perm_min_val <- if (has_perm) min(rer_df$p.perm, na.rm = TRUE) else NA_real_
perm_min_log10 <- if (!is.na(perm_min_val)) -log10(perm_min_val) else NA_real_
n_min_genes <- if (!is.na(perm_min_val)) sum(!is.na(rer_df$p.perm) & rer_df$p.perm == perm_min_val) else 0

p1 <- ggplot(rer_df, aes(x = -log10(P + 1e-300), y = -log10(p.perm))) +
  geom_point(aes(colour = case_when(
    pos_corr    ~ "Positively correlated",
    neg_corr    ~ "Negatively correlated",
    signif      ~ "Significant",
    TRUE        ~ "Non-significant"
  )), alpha = 0.7, size = 2) +
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, linetype = "dashed",
              colour = "grey40", linewidth = 0.5) +
  # Permutation significance threshold line
  geom_hline(yintercept = -log10(params$pval_threshold),
             linetype = "dotted", colour = "grey50", linewidth = 0.5) +
  # Line at the observed minimum (not a theoretical bound)
  {if (!is.na(perm_min_log10))
     geom_hline(yintercept = perm_min_log10,
                linetype = "solid", colour = "#d62728", linewidth = 0.5, alpha = 0.6)
   else list()} +
  {if (!is.na(perm_min_log10) && n_min_genes > 0)
     annotate("text", x = Inf, y = perm_min_log10,
              label = sprintf(" observed minimum: p = %.4f  (%d genes)", perm_min_val, n_min_genes),
              hjust = 1.05, vjust = -0.4, size = 3, colour = "#d62728")
   else list()} +
  geom_text_repel(data = perm_label_df, aes(label = gene),
                  size = 2.8, max.overlaps = 25) +
  scale_colour_manual(
    values = c(
      "Positively correlated" = .tableau10[3],
      "Negatively correlated" = .tableau10[1],
      "Significant"           = .tableau10[2],
      "Non-significant"       = "grey60"
    ), name = NULL
  ) +
  labs(
    title    = "Parametric (raw P) vs empirical (p.perm) significance",
    subtitle = paste0("Trait: ", params$traitname,
                     " | Dashed diagonal = equal evidence"),
    x = expression(-log[10](P)),
    y = expression(-log[10](p.perm))
  ) +
  report_theme(base_size = 13) +
  theme(legend.position = "top")

# Histogram: highlight genes exactly at the observed minimum.
perm_df_hist <- rer_df %>%
  filter(!is.na(p.perm)) %>%
  mutate(at_minimum = !is.na(perm_min_val) & p.perm == perm_min_val)

p2 <- ggplot(perm_df_hist, aes(x = p.perm, fill = at_minimum)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 50, colour = "white", alpha = 0.85) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = params$pval_threshold,
             linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey40", linewidth = 0.7) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c(`FALSE` = .tableau10[5], `TRUE` = "#d62728"),
    labels = c(`FALSE` = "Observed p.perm", `TRUE` = sprintf("Observed minimum (p = %.4f)", if (!is.na(perm_min_val)) perm_min_val else 0)),
    name   = NULL
  ) +
  labs(
    title    = "Distribution of permutation p-values",
    subtitle = if (n_min_genes > 0) sprintf("%d genes at the observed minimum (p.perm = %.4f)", n_min_genes, perm_min_val) else NULL,
    x = "p.perm",
    y = "Number of genes"
  ) +
  report_theme(base_size = 13) +
  theme(legend.position = "top")

gridExtra::grid.arrange(p1, p2, ncol = 2)
```

## Empirical BH evidence

```{r empirical-bh, results="asis"}
if (!has_perm) {
  cat("Empirical evidence unavailable; neither nominal nor BH calls can be made.\n")
} else {
  pv <- sort(rer_df$p.perm[!is.na(rer_df$p.perm)])
  m <- length(pv)
  bh_candidates <- m * pv / seq_along(pv)
  j <- which.min(bh_candidates)
  cat(sprintf("BH family: **%d available genes**; **%d unavailable**. Nominal calls: **%d** (positive **%d**, negative **%d**). BH calls at %g: **%d**.\n\n",
              m, sum(is.na(rer_df$p.perm)), sum(rer_df$signif),
              sum(rer_df$pos_corr, na.rm=TRUE), sum(rer_df$neg_corr, na.rm=TRUE),
              params$fdr_threshold, sum(rer_df$signif_perm_fdr)))
  cat(sprintf("Minimum adjusted empirical p: **%.10g**. The smallest BH candidate m × p / rank is %.10g at rank %d (p = %.10g). BH uses the cumulative minimum from larger ranks; this depends on the full p distribution, not just its minimum.\n\n",
              min(rer_df$p.perm.adj, na.rm=TRUE), bh_candidates[j], j, pv[j]))
  cat("No BH calls means insufficient evidence at the selected family-wide cutoff; it does not prove no biological association.\n")
}
```

## Directional nominal calls {.tabset}

Both tabs use **p.perm < `r params$pval_threshold`**, before BH. Each shows at most
`r params$top_n_labels` genes; the full calls are in the gene-level table and TSV.
BH status is displayed separately. No empirical p-values means no nominal calls.

### Positively correlated genes

```{r top-positive, results="asis"}
sort_col <- if (has_perm) "p.perm" else "p.adj"

top_pos <- rer_df %>%
  filter(pos_corr) %>%
  arrange(.data[[sort_col]], desc(Rho)) %>%
  slice_head(n = params$top_n_labels) %>%
  mutate(Rho = round(Rho, 4), p.adj = signif(p.adj, 3))

if (has_perm) {
  top_pos <- top_pos %>%
    mutate(p.perm = fmt_pperm(p.perm), p.perm.adj = signif(p.perm.adj, 3)) %>%
    select(gene, Rho, N, p.adj, p.perm, p.perm.adj, `BH empirical`)
  col_names <- c("Gene", "Rho", "N", "p.adj (parametric BH)", "p.perm (nominal)", "p.perm.adj (BH)", "BH empirical")
} else {
  top_pos <- top_pos %>% select(gene, Rho, N, p.adj)
  col_names <- c("Gene", "Rho", "N", "p.adj (parametric BH)")
}

if (nrow(top_pos) == 0) {
  cat("No positive nominal empirical calls (evidence unavailable or no genes below the nominal threshold).\n")
} else {
  knitr::kable(
    top_pos,
    col.names = col_names,
    row.names = FALSE,
    caption   = "Positive nominal calls: higher RER associated with more positive phenotype changes (continuous mode)"
  )
}
```

### Negatively correlated genes

```{r top-negative, results="asis"}
top_neg <- rer_df %>%
  filter(neg_corr) %>%
  arrange(.data[[sort_col]], Rho) %>%
  slice_head(n = params$top_n_labels) %>%
  mutate(Rho = round(Rho, 4), p.adj = signif(p.adj, 3))

if (has_perm) {
  top_neg <- top_neg %>%
    mutate(p.perm = fmt_pperm(p.perm), p.perm.adj = signif(p.perm.adj, 3)) %>%
    select(gene, Rho, N, p.adj, p.perm, p.perm.adj, `BH empirical`)
} else {
  top_neg <- top_neg %>% select(gene, Rho, N, p.adj)
}

if (nrow(top_neg) == 0) {
  cat("No negative nominal empirical calls (evidence unavailable or no genes below the nominal threshold).\n")
} else {
  knitr::kable(
    top_neg,
    col.names = col_names,
    row.names = FALSE,
    caption   = "Negative nominal calls: higher RER associated with more negative phenotype changes (continuous mode)"
  )
}
```

## Methods

**Tool:** RERconverge (Kowalczyk _et al._, 2019, _Bioinformatics_ 35:4815;
https://github.com/nclark-lab/RERconverge) via the correlation function for the recorded analysis mode.
Continuous mode uses `correlateWithContinuousPhenotype()`; binary mode uses
`correlateWithBinaryPhenotype()` with its recorded foreground-clade policy. Permulations: Saputra _et al._ 2021, _Mol. Biol. Evol._ 38:3004, doi:10.1093/molbev/msab068.

**Trait:** `r params$traitname`

**RER computation:** Relative evolutionary rates were calculated with `getAllResiduals()` using
a square-root branch-length transform and scaling (`transform="sqrt"`, `norm="scale"`).
The current matrix producer requires `use.weights=TRUE`; technical failures abort.
Legacy results without matrix metadata have unknown effective weighting. Association statistics are unavailable when the gene has fewer matched non-missing paths than `min.sp`; rows are retained as NA.

```{r recorded-settings, results='asis'}
if (is.null(.settings)) { cat('Original inference settings: **unknown**.\n') } else {
  visible <- .settings
  # The full path/gene rosters and checksums remain in the saved metadata.
  if (!is.null(visible$matrix_contract)) {
    mc <- visible$matrix_contract
    visible$matrix <- c(mc[intersect(c('use.weights','transform','norm','min.sp','package_version'),names(mc))],
                       list(genes=length(mc$genes),paths=length(mc$paths)))
    visible$matrix_contract <- NULL
  }
  if (!is.null(visible$trait_metadata)) visible$trait_metadata <- visible$trait_metadata[
    intersect(c('requested_mode','mode','binary_encoding'),names(visible$trait_metadata))]
  if (!is.null(visible$simulation_tree)) visible$simulation_tree$sha256 <- NULL
  cat('<pre>',htmltools::htmlEscape(jsonlite::toJSON(visible,pretty=TRUE,auto_unbox=TRUE,null='null',digits=NA)),'</pre>')
}
```

**Winsorization:** RER and trait values were optionally winsorized to reduce the influence of extreme values
(via `winsorizeRER` and `winsorizetrait` parameters).

**Effective trait transformation recorded for these data:** `r params$trait_transform`.
`r if (params$trait_transform == "ha_logit") "Haldane–Anscombe corrected logit: log((c + 0.5)/(n − c + 0.5)), where c is the case count and n the sample count. The raw prevalence is replaced by this count-based quantity before ancestral reconstruction. Correction depends on n as well as prevalence and can change the ordering of species." else if (params$trait_transform == "unknown") "Transformation was not supplied; verify the producing command before interpreting the phenotype scale." else "Consult the producing command and transformation settings; auto is a requested mode, not a recorded transformation outcome."`

**Statistical inference:** In continuous mode, Pearson correlation of gene RER and phenotype
paths after the configured winsorization. Native winsorization clips the specified number of
observations at each end; it is not a standard-deviation rule.
Nominal calls use **p.perm < `r params$pval_threshold`**; BH empirical calls use
**p.perm.adj < `r params$fdr_threshold`**. With no empirical evidence both are unavailable;
analytic results are displayed without substituting analytic calls into empirical lists.

**Permutation statistics:** `r if (has_perm) paste0("Available gene empirical p-values: ", sum(!is.na(rer_df$p.perm)), "; unavailable: ", sum(is.na(rer_df$p.perm)), ". Recorded total cycles: ", if (length(n_perms_total)) n_perms_total else "not stored", ".") else "Empirical p-values unavailable."`
The continuous producer uses Brownian-motion simulations to assign the observed transformed
values by simulated ranks (`simpermvec`), preserving their distribution. The local generator
uses identical correlation settings for observed and null paths. Null rho batches are concatenated
for each gene before native `permpvalcor()`; p-values are not averaged between batches and
`combinePermData()` is not used by this producer. NA observed rho or an empty valid null gives
NA empirical p. With d observations on the selected side, the smallest possible value is
1/(d+1) when k=0; d need not equal half the configured cycles if there are NA or median ties.

**References:** [RERconverge source and documentation](https://github.com/nclark-lab/RERconverge),
[Saputra et al. 2021](https://doi.org/10.1093/molbev/msab068), and
[Redlich et al. 2024](https://doi.org/10.1093/molbev/msae210).
Redlich's categorical omnibus test is unsigned and uses an upper tail; its signed post hoc
tests and this continuous association have distinct estimands. The supplement's pathway
filters (analytic adjusted p < 0.15 plus empirical p < 0.025) do not redefine the gene BH cutoff.
